provenance: Cases where an emoji's meaning depends on which vendor renders it, or where a vendor's redesign changed the meaning in flight. These are documented design changes, not folk usage.

🔫.sense: water pistol on every major platform
🔫.gloss: Apple changed its realistic revolver to a green water pistol in iOS 10 (2016); Samsung, Twitter, Google, Microsoft, Facebook and WhatsApp all followed by 2018. The Unicode name remains 'pistol', so the glyph's name and its universal appearance no longer agree.

🍑.gloss: Apple's iOS 10 beta made the peach flatter and more fruit-like; the change was reversed before release after users objected that it broke the euphemism.

🤝.gloss: The single-glyph handshake could not take two different tones. Emoji 14.0 added 🫱🏻‍🫲🏽 as a ZWJ sequence specifically to allow it.

🥲.gloss: Some vendors draw a single tear and a broad smile, others a barely-there tear, which shifts the emoji between 'bravely coping' and 'genuinely fine'.

😬.gloss: Rendered anywhere from mild awkwardness to outright terror depending on platform, a long-standing source of cross-device misreading.

🙃.sense: no upside-down variant of other faces
🙃.gloss: The only inverted face in the set, which is why it carries the whole burden of sarcasm.

☺️.gloss: Defaults to monochrome text rendering unless followed by U+FE0F, so it often appears as a black-and-white outline where authors expected colour.

❤️.gloss: U+2764 alone is a text-presentation dingbat. Only U+2764 U+FE0F renders as the familiar red heart, which is why hearts sometimes arrive as flat black glyphs.

#️⃣.gloss: A three-code-point sequence of digit, variation selector and combining enclosing keycap. Frequently mistaken for the hashtag character.

🏳️‍🌈.gloss: On systems lacking the sequence it breaks into a white flag followed by a rainbow, which reads very differently from the intended pride flag.

🏳️‍⚧️.gloss: The transgender flag, added in Emoji 13.0, still degrades to flag-plus-symbol on older systems.

🇺🇳.gloss: The UN flag is a regional-indicator pair like national flags, but UN is not an ISO country code in the ordinary sense; some pickers omit it.

🏴󠁧󠁢󠁳󠁣󠁴󠁿.gloss: Scotland is a seven-code-point tag sequence. Only England, Scotland and Wales exist as RGI tag flags, and unsupported systems show a plain black flag.

👨‍👩‍👧‍👦.gloss: Where the ZWJ sequence is unsupported, the family renders as four separate people standing in a row.

🧑‍🤝‍🧑.gloss: Built from neutral person glyphs specifically to avoid the gendered defaults of older couple emoji.

⚧️.gloss: The transgender symbol exists independently of the flag sequence and is often used alone as an identity marker.

🫯.gloss: The 'fight cloud' was added in Emoji 17.0 (September 2025), so on many devices it still appears as a tofu box. New emoji stay practically unusable for months or years after standardisation.

🫪.gloss: The 'distorted face', another Emoji 17.0 addition; expect missing-glyph boxes on systems that have not shipped the new font.

‼️.gloss: Predates emoji entirely as a typographic mark, which is why it needs U+FE0F to render in colour.

©️.gloss: The copyright sign is emoji-presentable but semantically a legal mark; its inclusion is a compatibility artefact of Japanese carrier sets.

®️.gloss: As with ©️, a legacy compatibility inclusion rather than a designed pictograph.

™️.gloss: Same legacy status; also used online as an ironic suffix marking a phrase as a branded cliché.
